thread:
kevin.prod: Hey team — getting 401s for a handful of requests after tenant migration this morning. Only on prod worker.
kevin.prod: Nginx shows: `{"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found for org 'org:old-123'"}}`
kevin.prod: Same API key works locally if I curl directly from my laptop.
support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-5643 — assigned to @mike_support
mike_support: Can you paste the exact curl (sanitise keys)? Also which header middleware sets?
kevin.prod: curl (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_redacted" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Org: org:old-123" \
  -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
```
kevin.prod: If I drop `X-Redwood-Org` it returns 200. With header, 401.
ankur: We do org-bound key validation for Private/org-scoped keys. If header is present we verify it matches the binding; mismatch => invalid_api_key.
mike_support: Did the migration touch the edge sidecar or proxy that might be injecting old tenant ids?
kevin.prod: Yes — we deployed a migration proxy yesterday that rewrites routing headers for legacy tenants.
kevin.prod: Dashboard shows key is bound to `org:prod-987`.
kevin.prod: Quick test: updated proxy to set `X-Redwood-Org: org:prod-987` and retried — calls succeed.
mike_support: Perfect. Root cause: proxy left old tenant id in X-Redwood-Org causing org-key mismatch => 401 invalid_api_key.
ankur: Short term: remove header or fix proxy mapping. Long term: ensure migration writes correct tenant or omit header for org-bound keys.
mike_support: Adding KB: "org header mismatch from migration proxy can result in invalid_api_key 401" (refs PR #482).
kevin.prod: Deployed fix, verified, all green. Thanks :raised_hands:
support-bot: Ticket #SUP-5643 closed by @mike_support
